newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT plans to hike long distance call rates.
newsitem.headline: PLDT plans to hike long distance call rates.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) is planning to raise its long distance call rates, possibly by September, following the peso's sharp depreciation, a PLDT official said on Wednesday.

"We are still looking at the range for the increase. It could be 10 percent, 20 percent or 30 percent. It will all depend on how it will affect our internal targets and what's fair for our subscribers," the PLDT finance official told reporters. "Maybe it will take effect by September."
He said telephone firms are allowed to adjust domestic long distance rates without prior approval from the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC).
Under an NTC memorandum issued in 1983, telephone companies are allowed a one-percent adjustment in long distance rates for every 10 centavo movement in the value of the peso against the U.S. dollar.
On Wednesday, the peso fell more than 10 percent to close at 29.30 to the dollar. The peso has been dropping sharply since the Philippine central bank announced a de facto devaluation on Friday.
PLDT's pricing division head Miguela Villanueva said in a separate interview that PLDT would notify the NTC shortly of its intention to increase the rates.
The company can implement the rate adjustment 15 days after its submission.
